title: Trumpet styles, Chris Kelly, and the E. Gibson band personnel
summary: Lawn parties, trumpet playing style and features, then who is in the E. Gibson band now and how little dance work they get.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: out. Were they still having any lawn parties?

No, they're not having. I haven't heard of a lawn party in years. No, I think that would be a good drawing feature if they'd start to give them a few lawn parties. In the summertime, that's because that's out in openings. So the wintertime, this kind of, in the winter season come out, lawn parties just out. It's mostly for the summer. You know, somebody else I wanted to ask you about was Tom Anderson's Place. You mentioned that. Yeah. You said you were down by there, huh? Uh-huh. Did you play in any- Oh you mean in the French Quarters? Yeah. Well in the district, yeah. Yeah. I'm trying to think of a musician that used to be out there. He's a trumpet player. Yeah. Well what did he play like? That's a trumpet player. Yeah, but I mean did he play a lot of high notes or in the staff? Well you see, when you catch the most of trumpet players, like when there's one trumpet in a band, he mostly used, the most he did use was six and seven pieces. Well you take a trumpet player like that, he's even there by himself, he'd play in the staff and over the staff too. Yeah. A long time ago when he'd be fixing to play the ending of a number, he'd mostly go over the staff. He'd play the staff. Oh that's something I wanted to ask you, that reminds me. What special numbers did these trumpet players feature around here? Were there any numbers like say Buddy and Renee, what would they feature? Well they played like the sunny side of the streets. Did they have any real crips? Well they did, but I can't remember the name of them because that was most of their specials, and that was most of the band or the musicians that was playing with them know what they were going to play. They'd say let's play an old number, they'd call any number, probably make the name themselves, and just go on and feature. What did Chris Kelly feature? The trumpet? No I mean tunes. Oh well like I said, Chris would play over the staff, in the staff. Yeah. He was a hot man. But did he play marches or blues or what? Yeah he played both. He was a mixer in music. He played every kind of tune. Yeah he played every kind. I see. Well when you got well and up again and got back in music, who did you join up with? Well I started playing with the E. Gibson band. And I'm playing with them right now. And who's in that band? Well the manager is Spears. And we have another trumpet player, his name is Johnny. John McNeil. John McNeil and Johnny. Oh Johnny, I know. Oh I know, John Wembley. Yeah, yeah that's right. And we have Dave Bailey on bass drums. We have Calvin on trombone. Cal Blunt. Yeah. And we have another trombone player. I can't call his name right now. I'd have to look in my book for his name. Do you have your book with you? No I don't have my book with me. Freddie Miller was there Sunday. Does he play steady with you Freddie? That's him, yeah. He's got Red's trombone. That's him. Yeah, that's Freddie. That's something you know. It's got a five and a half inch bell and it's got a real long bell. It goes away. Chris Balber told me that's a military style trombone. That English trombone player told me that. It is? Says it's a military style, military band. But it gives a nice tone. Yeah it's got a nice tone to it. Let's see, Freddie, Cal, Leon was there on trumpet too Sunday. Yeah. Well in the place of MacNeil, that's who they're using now, Moses, Leon, on trumpet. And we use as Keppert on the bass. Louis Keppert. Louis Keppert. And the snare drummer is who? George Sterling was there. Sterling, that's right. Is he a regular man? Yeah, he's a regular. And Davis on saxophone. What's his first name? I don't know him. On alto. I don't know him. No, I can't call him Davis. Sometimes Lawrence Dent used to play with you. Well, sometimes he'd get in there. Dent plays. He plays clarinet and sax. Let's see, Leon was playing trumpet too sometimes. I'm trying to remember who I've seen through the years with the Gibsons. They had some young kids too from time to time. Eddie Morris too. You know Eddie Morris. Yeah, well that was Eddie Morris. That's an old musician. Yeah, well he used to be with the Gibsons. He played a couple of jobs with the Gibsons. But I don't know what happened. I think Eddie got better jobs. With more study and of course he couldn't be with the Gibsons band then after that happened. Well when you were playing with the Eureka and the Gibsons all through those recent years, did you play any much dance work? No. Since I've been playing with the Gibsons band we played I believe one dance. All the most they do is parades. But you wouldn't go out with other bands and play dances. If I would get an offer I would. But I just, things just sewed up like that. I couldn't get anything else. They're hard. Time to hard.
